assumptions: Path C: one coherent spec, the seal stage's syntax check for JavaScript test files.

Feature flow (a new seal check); the task text fixes the approach (node --check in seal.ts), so the variant pick was not put to the orchestrator. Rejected: the check through o.run (scripted runners answer unknown commands red; the shell runner depends on PATH) and an in-process vm parse (ESM needs --experimental-vm-modules).
Ships as a patch bump 0.29.1 with a CHANGELOG entry under Fixed, per merge_obligations in .marvin/config.json; manifests, dist/ and catalog.json are scope.exempt by-products.

The check runs with process.execPath (the engine's node), not `node` on PATH, with cwd set to the worktree and bounded by timeoutMs. It checks the file in place so that a .js file's module type comes from its nearest package.json.
A check that cannot run (spawn error, signal, timeout) refuses the file instead of sealing it unchecked (AC7).
Extensions are matched exactly (.js, .mjs, .cjs); a .js file in a JSX or Flow dialect is refused, because the task names .js explicitly.
The test-author's F2 raises the seal test helper's default timeoutMs, and the D-RESEAL test's explicit value, from 1000 to 60000 so that the new spawn is not cut short under load.
Host conventions read from .marvin/config.json: gates.test_one `node scripts/test-one.mjs {file}` runs every kind:test oracle; test_command is the configured `test` gate.
No engine, runtime or role-prompt change: runtime.ts:1636 and engine.ts:883 already return seal reasons to the test-author as findings.
Spec critic pass 2 returned PASS WITH WARNINGS with two warnings unlisted; accepted without seeing them.
